messages:
Ana (AE): Heads-up — NorthForge wants to POC their nf-65b-adapter model. Main asks: kv-cache compatibility (we use sticky sessions), quantization variant support, pricing for a 50 rps POC for 2 weeks, and KMS + data flow Qs. Can SE/ML weigh in? cc @Ravi @Maya @Sam

Ravi (SE): Quick read — adapter looks like a fairly standard transformer with rotary embeddings. Need to confirm RMSNorm vs LayerNorm; if it's RMSNorm we have kernels but might fallback in some ops. For kv-cache: should be fine but want to run the variant compatibility scanner. Suggest we try nf-65b-q4f16 and nf-65b-q8_0 variants for perf/quality checks. If they need 250ms p50 at 50 rps, Dedicated pool recommended.

Maya (ML Eng): Agree with Ravi. Also need expected sequence length distribution — if typical >1024 the cache layout and memory will change perf. Can you ask NorthForge for typical prompt+context size? For quality checks I'll run our eval harness once we have weights or HF repo.

Ravi (SE): I'll queue the compatibility scanner. Two quick notes: 1) if the model includes a custom attention kernel we'll need a kernel patch (adds ~1 week); 2) please provide config.json + sample input so tokenizer/shape checks pass.

Jordan (NorthForge): Jordan here — our avg seq is ~720 tokens, peaks ~2k for some long-chat use cases (rare). We can provide the HF repo link and a small sample corpus. Latency target 250ms p50. POC start ideally next Mon.

Maya (ML Eng): 720 typical is good. 2k peaks mean we should enable dynamic padding and an eviction policy for the KV. For 250ms p50 at 720 typical, q4f16 on Dedicated (A100 equiv) should be fine with proper batching settings. I'll prepare recommended batch/window settings after the baseline.

Chris (SalesOps): Rough POC pricing for 2 weeks: estimate a small Dedicated pool (2x A100 equiv) as baseline => ~$6,800/week + metered token costs. If they prefer hosted, per-token costs are higher for the same perf. I'll draft a formal quote and include burst pricing.

Sam (Security): KMS integration is supported for Dedicated/Private (BYOK). We'll need: full security questionnaire answered, a data-flow diagram, and confirmation on where model weights will be hosted. Note: we don't move customer model weights to public S3; recommend private registry or SFTP. Also request SOC2 report and IP terms for weight handling.

Ana (AE): Action items: I'll collect HF link, sample, and eval set and upload to the compatibility-run doc. @Ravi can you add the scanner results by Fri EOD? @Chris please draft quote including burst and reserved options. @Sam I'll send the security questionnaire and request KMS contact.

Ravi (SE): Will do. KVCACHE note: if they want cross-request KV sharing across instances we need sticky routing; otherwise consistent hashing with cache warmup is OK. Scanner will flag any custom ops.

deploy-bot: compatibility-scan-job-6234567890 queued by Ravi. Status: queued

Jordan (NorthForge): Also: confirm tokenizer — we use SentencePiece BPE. We can also export quantized weights if that helps testing.

Maya (ML Eng): SentencePiece is fine. If they export quantized weights we can skip quantization and focus on perf/accuracy checks, but we'll still run our evals. Please include a small hallucination/regression eval set.

Ana (AE): Plan summary: 1) customer sends HF link + sample + eval set + KMS contact; 2) SE runs compatibility scan + perf baseline; 3) Security completes questionnaire; 4) SalesOps sends formal quote. Kickoff next Mon. Sound good?

Jordan (NorthForge): Sounds good — I'll send everything by EOD tomorrow.

Ravi (SE): Noted. FYI if scanner flags a custom op we'll need an extra week for kernel work.

Maya (ML Eng): I'll queue the evals once repo is in. /cc @Chris on token estimates for billing.

Chris (SalesOps): Added a line item for embeddings+reranking demo (placeholder) — I'll finalize numbers after the scan.

Ana (AE): Thanks team :thumbsup:
